headline: High data-leakage risk: great_expectations can handle files while opik has broad network egress, creating a default path for sensitive validation data to leave the workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: great_expectations reads and writes files, so if opik outputs are manually or programmatically fed into its validation inputs, prompt-like content could influence downstream processing. However, no shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented, and opik only exposes REST API calls. This is a plausible but not default bridge.
conditions: IF opik outputs are copied into great_expectations input files without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from any text passed into validation files.
Use a fixed schema for inputs and reject free-form text.
Review any copied output before saving it as a file.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: great_expectations touches data sources, validation results, and documentation files, while opik has broad network egress and REST API access. If sensitive validation artifacts are routed from A into B, B can transmit them off-host. The pair does not show a shared workspace by default, so this is not high, but the leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF validation results or source data are passed from great_expectations into opik, leakage becomes possible.
IF opik sends those artifacts to a remote REST endpoint, the data leaves the local environment.
mitigations: Do not pass raw data files into opik.
Redact validation outputs before upload.
Disable network access for opik in sensitive runs.
Use a local-only test dataset.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and content filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: great_expectations can install packages and write files, while opik can call REST APIs and has broad egress. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap on the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because no shared filesystem, git state, or OAuth scope is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable API credentials, overlapping writes may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid sharing API credentials between agents.
Run one agent at a time for mutable tasks.
Use lock files for any shared artifact.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: great_expectations produces validation results that opik could ingest for evaluation or reporting. If opik treats those outputs as authoritative without a verification step, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream judgments or actions. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, not directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF opik consumes great_expectations validation results as ground truth, cascading error is possible.
IF downstream automation acts on those results without human review, impact increases.
mitigations: Require a human review step before acting on validation results.
Cross-check results against a second source.
Mark generated outputs as untrusted metadata.
Keep evaluation reports separate from operational decisions.
requires-engineering: add explicit verification gates in the pipeline.

E_compliance.rationale: great_expectations handles data quality tests, validation results, and documentation, which may include regulated data classes, while opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern is supportable from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in validation artifacts and sent through opik, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those artifacts, the mismatch becomes material.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from validation runs.
Anonymize documentation and results before sharing.
Keep sensitive artifacts local.
Review retention settings for any uploaded reports.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for the pipeline.
